What to look for in this update

- The setup changed: the lead hand is turned more on top (3 knuckles), the lead wrist cupped about 31° (Riley 25–28°). Compare "address a57k" (new) with "address a45s" (old). - Takeaway to 0.25 s, D57_B: the face now points at the ball line at shaft-parallel, but the lead wrist goes from cupped to bowed (about 48°) to get there, and the forearm rolls open. By 0.33 s the face is about 28° open again. - D57_LA0 / LA2: the "ball between the elbows" keeps the elbows 2–3 cm closer than LA0x. With the lift (LA2) the lead arm reaches its across-the-chest limit just before the top. The trail arm ends folded in front of the chest on every swing. - Not touched: the transition, the downswing and the head (that runs next, as 0058). Every swing stops just after the top. - Numbers only: EGS's forearm set (D57_FS) keeps the forearm from rolling open and closes the face 2–3° at shaft-parallel and about 7° by 0.33 s. The shoulder blades hit their limits early under the elbow tension; that is a model issue, not a move to look for. — researcher 0057
